groups.title: Capsule (153101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have liver cirrhosis or cystathionine synthase deficiency; if you have peptic ulcer; or if you have severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 25 mL/min) or severe liver impairment.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF.

Do not take it continuously for 10 days or more for an acute respiratory condition.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a cough medicine.

If headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Loosening mucus and helping to bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease

groups.title: Oral Suspension (227730ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to remove bubbles in the bowel during gastroscopy, to remove gas in the bowel during abdominal X-ray examination, and to improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract (a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, aerophagia and the like).
groups.usage: To remove bubbles in the bowel for gastroscopy, adults: take 40 to 80 mg with about 10 mL of water 15 to 40 minutes before the examination. To remove gas in the bowel for abdominal X-ray examination, adults: take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or between meals, starting 3 to 4 days before the examination. To improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract, adults: take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or at bedtime. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have asthma.

Shake it well before use.

Occasionally loose stools, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea, a feeling of heaviness in the abdomen or loss of appetite, and rarely headache or mild irritation of the skin, eyes or mucous membranes may occur.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (142301ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have bronchial asthma; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you are in early pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant; or if you have had a gastrointestinal ulcer caused by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine in the past.

Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

While you are taking this medicine, do not use another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you use it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (for example a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim or heparin), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis or bronchospasm; rarely a risk of acute pneumonia in people with heart failure; visual disturbance such as loss of vision or scotoma, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, acute renal failure, reduced urine output or blood in the urine, and protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, acute pulmonary oedema, peripheral oedema, fluid retention, reduced fertility in women, swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

groups.title: Syrup (A80500ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Ages 15 years and older: take 15 mL per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 10 mL per dose. Ages 7 years to under 11 years: take 7.5 mL per dose. Ages 3 years to under 7 years: take 5 mL per dose. Ages 2 years to under 3 years: take 3.75 mL per dose. Take it 3 to 4 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals and at bedtime.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have a constitution prone to allergy; if you have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening, and severe symptoms such as burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), or cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Capsule (D82200ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, oedema, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or if you take it together with a potassium-containing preparation, a liquorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide), or flucloxacillin. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, or rarely shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (high fever with rash and reddening and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever), reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, raised blood pressure, headache, or myopathy (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (531500ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes caused by a nasal cold and by allergic and vasomotor rhinitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 10 mL per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to methyl parahydroxybenzoate; if you have severe liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have severe heart disease; if you have difficulty passing urine with residual urine; if you have high blood pressure or coronary artery disease; if you are being given an MAO inhibitor; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if the user is a baby aged 2 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 12 years of age, or if you have asthma, glaucoma, heart disease or arrhythmia, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia.

Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor, a blood-pressure-lowering medicine, alcohol, a central nervous system depressant (hypnotic, sedative, tranquilliser), a sympathomimetic, a tricyclic antidepressant, guanethidine, bretylium, bethanidine, debrisoquine, methyldopa, a sympathomimetic medicine (decongestant, appetite suppressant, amphetamine-type stimulant) or an adrenergic blocker.

If sedation, drowsiness, central nervous system depression, central stimulation, anxiety, sweating, a mild fall in blood pressure, visual disturbance, dilated pupils, delirium, hallucination, excitement, muscle cramps, stiffness, athetosis, clonic and tonic convulsions, high fever, respiratory paralysis, coma, circulatory collapse, skin reactions, temporary stinging pain, a burning sensation, thirst, nausea, vomiting, difficulty passing urine, excitement, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction (fever, erythema, many small pustules and the like), ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like), or symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (347904ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of runny nose, sneezing, itching and watering of the eyes, and itching of the nose or throat caused by pollen allergy or other upper respiratory tract allergy.
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose with water, at intervals of 12 hours. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if you are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 12 years of age; if you have kidney impairment; if you are an older person aged 65 years and older; if you do not know whether the symptoms are caused by allergic rhinitis, a cold or another cause; if you have been diagnosed with an allergic disease (bronchial asthma, atopic dermatitis and the like); if nasal congestion is severe; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person; if you have had an allergy caused by a medicine; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have cardiovascular disease.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with another anti-allergy medicine (including medicines for skin disease and oral medicines for rhinitis), an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (cold medicine, antitussive-expectorant, motion-sickness medicine, hypnotic sedative and the like), an antacid (preparations containing aluminium or magnesium), ketoconazole or erythromycin. Do not take it with fruit juices such as grapefruit juice, orange juice or apple juice, or with food. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If dry mouth, constipation, diarrhoea, drowsiness, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips, rash, itching, urticaria, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, numbness, headache, fatigue, lassitude, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness, nightmares, sleep disturbance, frequent urination, difficulty passing urine, palpitations, taste disturbance, oedema, chest pain, difficulty breathing, raised blood pressure or menstrual disturbance occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, signs of shock occur (itching of the skin, urticaria, hoarseness, sneezing, itching of the throat, difficulty breathing, palpitations or clouding of consciousness soon after taking it), or if jaundice (yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes), brown urine, general lassitude, loss of appetite, a fall in blood pressure, angioedema, chest pain, flushing, raised AST, ALT, gamma-GTP, ALP or LDH, dizziness or frequent nausea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If agranulocytosis, reduced white blood cells or neutropenia occurs with sudden high fever, chills or sore throat, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (101804ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For an acute condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For a chronic condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis, ages 6 years and older: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 2 years of age; if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If you take it together with an oral antibiotic (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If, rarely, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, ringing in the ears, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), rapid heartbeat or high blood pressure occurs, or very rarely anaphylaxis occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (106331ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbance of mucus secretion.
groups.usage: Adults: at the start of treatment take 30 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day; when treatment is continued take 15 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Children aged 5 years and older: take 15 mg per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. Ages 2 to 4 years: take 7.5 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day. It may be taken with or without food.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment, or if you have a hereditary predisposition to fructose intolerance.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or peptic ulcer; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you are an older person; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: new damage to the skin or mucous membranes, fever, itching, rhinitis, and non-specific influenza-like prodromal symptoms such as cough and sore throat; commonly nausea or reduced sensation in the mouth; uncommonly vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain, heartburn or dry mouth; rarely dryness of the throat, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, constipation or loss of appetite; rarely urticaria, skin rash, a severe acute anaphylactic reaction (including anaphylactic shock), urticarial erythema, angioedema, itching or other hypersensitivity reactions, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, or a rise in body temperature with chills; commonly reduced sensation in the pharynx; very rarely purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count; commonly taste disturbance (for example a change in taste); uncommonly abnormal sensation of the tongue; rarely a feeling of numbness in the arm.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (292800ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 to 3 tablets per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose. Take it 1 time in 1 day at bedtime (or on an empty stomach). For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger; if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel); or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5; or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not chew the tablet when taking it. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Children under 15 years of age must not take this medicine.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to another antihistamine, a motion-sickness medicine, a cold medicine or an antitussive-expectorant; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have difficulty passing urine such as prostatic hyperplasia; or if you have glaucoma or have had heart disease.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with a motion-sickness medicine, a cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, an antitussive-expectorant or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (medicine for rhinitis or allergy).

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, difficulty passing urine, raised blood pressure, dry mouth, constipation or diarrhoea occurs, or if, rarely, signs of aplastic anaemia (bruising, nosebleed, bleeding gums, fever, pale skin and mucous membranes, fatigue, palpitations, difficulty breathing, anaemia, blood in the urine) or signs of agranulocytosis (sudden high fever, chills, sore throat) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (104303ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the treatment of infection with roundworm, pinworm, hookworm (Ancylostoma), whipworm, American hookworm (Necator) and threadworm (Strongyloides), and of mixed infections with these worms.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 24 months and older: for pinworm, take 1 tablet (400 mg), 1 time in 1 day. To eradicate the infection, take 1 further tablet (400 mg) once more 7 days later. For roundworm, hookworm, whipworm and American hookworm, take 1 tablet (400 mg) as a single dose. For severe mixed infection of threadworm with another parasite (tapeworm), take 1 tablet (400 mg), 1 time in 1 day, for 3 days. If it is hard to swallow, the tablet may be chewed or taken with a small amount of water; no special measures such as stopping meals or using a laxative are needed. An examination is carried out 3 weeks after treatment, and if the infection has not been cured a second course may be given in some cases.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver impairment or kidney impairment, or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergy to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, cimetidine, praziquantel, dexamethasone, ritonavir, phenytoin, carbamazepine or phenobarbital.

If Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), erythema multiforme, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, diarrhoea, upper abdominal or abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, fever, generalised reddening of the skin, rash, itching, urticaria or another hypersensitivity reaction, or reversible hair loss occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (172806ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day; up to 8 tablets (3200 mg) may be taken in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis: take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not take more than the recommended dose. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are taking high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, or liver impairment now or in the past; if you have kidney impairment now or in the past; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, low-dose aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If an increased risk of myocardial infarction or stroke, or serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration or perforation occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or ALP, liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as blind spots, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); raised blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed or peripheral oedema.
